15.t: Working with data: a salt-marsh transect
q: Found only from 20 to 40 m, with most cover at 20 m (40%), where salinity is 28 g dm⁻³ and the soil is flooded 8 hours a day.
Explain why there are no plants at 0 m.
Flooded 12 hours a day by very salty water: plants lose water by osmosis, roots get little oxygen, and waves disturb the mud.
Suggest why glasswort is absent at 60–80 m, where conditions are less extreme.
It is outcompeted by grass and sea purslane there: its realised niche is smaller than its fundamental niche.
Explain why it is hard to say whether salinity or flooding controls the plants.
The two variables change together along the transect, so their effects cannot be separated; an experiment changing one at a time is needed.
Suggest two ways to make the transect results more reliable.
Any two: repeat transects at other places on the marsh; more quadrats at each point; take readings on several days.
